timeline.event: Harald Bluetooth raises the great runestone at Jelling
timeline.label: c. 965

timeline.event: Cnut the Great becomes King of England
Bishop Absalon founds Copenhagen
The Kalmar Union unites Denmark, Norway and Sweden
Denmark adopts the Lutheran Reformation
Tycho Brahe begins building his Uraniborg observatory on Hven
The Treaty of Roskilde cedes Skåne to Sweden
Frederick III introduces absolute monarchy
Denmark cedes Norway to Sweden in the Treaty of Kiel
Hans Christian Andersen publishes his first fairy tales
Frederick VII signs Denmark's first democratic constitution
Denmark loses Schleswig and Holstein after defeat at Dybbøl
The Little Mermaid statue is unveiled in Copenhagen
Northern Schleswig rejoins Denmark after a plebiscite
Ole Kirk Christiansen starts the Billund toy firm that becomes LEGO
German forces occupy Denmark
Denmark joins the European Economic Community
Denmark wins the European Football Championship
The Great Belt road bridge opens between Funen and Zealand
The Øresund Bridge links Copenhagen with Malmö

places.name: Copenhagen
places.clue: Founded around Bishop Absalon's fortress in 1167, the capital's name means "merchants' harbour".

places.name: Aarhus
places.clue: Denmark's second city is home to the ARoS art museum, crowned by a circular rainbow walkway.

places.name: Odense
places.clue: Hans Christian Andersen was born in this Funen city in 1805, and a museum here tells his story.

places.name: Skagen
places.clue: At Denmark's northern tip, where the Skagerrak meets the Kattegat, its light drew the 19th-century Skagen Painters.

places.name: Aalborg
places.clue: On the Limfjord, near the Viking burial ground of Lindholm Høje with its hundreds of stone-ringed graves.

places.name: Jelling
places.clue: Its runestones, raised by Gorm the Old and Harald Bluetooth, are often called Denmark's birth certificate.

places.name: Ribe
places.clue: Founded in the early 700s, this is generally considered Denmark's oldest town, on the edge of the Wadden Sea.

places.name: Møns Klint
places.clue: White chalk cliffs rising about 128 m above the Baltic, built from the shells of tiny ancient sea creatures.

places.name: Trelleborg
places.clue: A perfectly circular Viking ring fortress, built around 980 in the reign of Harald Bluetooth.

places.name: Dybbøl Mill
places.clue: This windmill stands on the hill where Prussian troops overran Denmark's defences on 18 April 1864.

places.name: Thy National Park
places.clue: Denmark's first national park, created in 2008, protects wild dunes and heaths along the North Sea coast.

places.name: Læsø
places.clue: A Kattegat island known for its medieval salt-boiling industry and old houses roofed with thick eelgrass.
